requirements.title: Progress separates completeness from usable shape
requirements.statement: Product status separately reports mature-contract completeness, stage readiness, and usable feature/journey closure or shape.
requirements.positive: Two fixtures with equal raw obligation ratio but different journey closure produce distinct shape/readiness outputs.
requirements.negative: A single percent-done field is insufficient as the sole product-state representation.

requirements.title: VP stages are semantic projections
requirements.statement: CVP/MVP/other stages select requirements, features, and journeys from the mature contract by coherent outcome/dependency rules.
requirements.positive: Every required stage obligation is justified by an outcome/dependency and blockers derive from that projection.
requirements.negative: Fixed percentages, requirement counts, or array positions must not determine stage membership.

requirements.title: Stage implementations expose transition debt
requirements.statement: Early usable stages prefer mature-shaped boundaries and explicitly classify temporary implementations whose later replacement/migration burden is nontrivial.
requirements.positive: Stage-critical stubs/adapters record disposition, consumers, and replacement/migration burden.
requirements.negative: Healthy transition readiness cannot be claimed while hiding required rewrites of the core spine.

requirements.title: Behavioral grade and trace completeness remain separate
requirements.statement: A requirement's behavioral result and completeness of specification/design/implementation/test/evidence trace links are independently represented.
requirements.positive: Represent a behaviorally failed but fully traced requirement and a verified but incompletely traced requirement without conflating states.
requirements.negative: Missing trace links must not fabricate a behavioral failure, and a passing behavior must not imply complete traceability.

requirements.title: Empty grading denominator is undefined
requirements.statement: A stage or requirement selection with no applicable graded obligations cannot produce a successful completion percentage or stage achievement.
requirements.positive: Grade an empty projection and receive undefined/not-assessable with explanation.

requirements.title: Implementation cannot silently weaken its own acceptance policy
requirements.statement: Changes to behavior cannot silently remove or weaken the acceptance policy used to grade that same behavior without separately authorized contract change.
requirements.positive: Modify implementation while retaining prior accepted criterion; failure remains visible until an independently accepted criterion revision exists.
requirements.negative: Deleting/fuzzing the failing check in the same implementation change must not manufacture green.

requirements.title: Scope delta reported separately from engineering progress
requirements.statement: Adding, retiring, or changing accepted obligations is reported independently from implementation/verification progress.
requirements.positive: Add a requirement to a new baseline and show scope increase separately from unchanged verified-work amount.
requirements.negative: Retiring requirements must not be reported as implementation work completed.

requirements.title: Auxiliary improvements do not inflate core functional completion
requirements.statement: Useful quality, UX, performance, maintenance, or optional-integration work is valued separately unless it satisfies an accepted functional obligation.
requirements.positive: Record a non-required UX improvement as auxiliary value with no core FR completion delta.
requirements.negative: Adding polish/integrations cannot increase core completion merely because work was substantial.

requirements.title: Usability derives from closed journeys
requirements.statement: Product usability/stage claims incorporate closure of declared actor-to-outcome journeys rather than inferring usability from primitive/file presence.
requirements.positive: A complete narrow end-to-end journey can yield vertical-slice shape even with limited mature breadth.
requirements.negative: Broad scaffolding with zero closed journeys must not be classified as an equivalent usable product.

requirements.title: Central registry projects repo-local truth
requirements.statement: PhenoRegistry summarizes and links Tracera's canonical repo-local contract/status without becoming a competing detailed source of truth.
requirements.positive: Update repo-local accepted contract then project identity/status/linkage into registry with revision reference.
requirements.negative: A stale registry summary must not override a newer accepted repo-local contract.
